items.text: The workmen were due on Monday. On Sunday night, a storm came in from the north.
items.speaker: narrator

items.text: Far out on the water, a small fishing boat was fighting its way home. On board, Mack Doyle could see nothing but rain and black waves.
items.speaker: narrator

items.text: Come on, old man. Where's your light?
items.speaker: mack

items.text: Then, through the rain, the beam swept over him, steady and bright, the way it had for forty years.
items.speaker: narrator

items.text: Mack's second line is relief, almost a whisper.
At dawn, the storm was gone. On the quay, the fishermen were waiting, and Clara was waiting with them.
items.speaker: narrator

items.text: You kept us alive last night, Tobias.
items.speaker: mack

items.text: They did not say much after that. They simply took off their caps, one by one, as the old keeper walked past. And for the rest of his life, whenever Tobias looked out to sea at night and saw the new light turning, he would smile, because he knew it was still his.
items.speaker: narrator
